Here’s a Widebody Lamborghini Temerario To Quench Your Tuned Supercar Thirst
21 photos
Photo: Instagram | kfletchphotography
The Lamborghini Temerario has already been visited by the tuning fairy multiple times, and it is not exactly a surprise, given that it debuted more than two years ago, at the 2024 Monterey Car Week, and it entered production at Sant’Agata Bolognese in 2025.
However, not many thing jobs managed to tick the cool and aggressive boxes at the same time. Sure, looks are definitely subjective, but to be honest, this model (and not only) is best left stock. That’s in my opinion, anyway, as my perfectly specced example would be bone stock, with a cool color on the outside, some Alcantara inserts in the cabin, and probably a new set of wheels.
And the latter would likely be where I would draw the line. You know, if I inherited a huge amount of money from a rich uncle I didn’t know existed, or I hit the jackpot, because this is one pricey ride. A brand new Lamborghini Temerario costs from roughly $400,000, but tick some boxes on the options list and get some Ad Personam goodies, and that price will easily climb to over half a million dollars.
Now, while my perfect Temerario would only feature aftermarket wheels, the one pictured in the gallery has much more than that. Images of it were shared by @kfletchphotography on Instagram earlier in the week, and the supercar features a widebody kit from 1016 Industries, AL13 wheels, and was assembled by RDB LA.
Photo: Instagram | kfletchphotography From what we can tell, the front bumper is the OEM element , but there are a few add-ons here that contribute to the supercar’s unique look. There is also a new splitter with blades on the sides, as well as a new hood that is on the more aggressive side of things. The front wheel arches feature some aftermarket elements on them in order to look more muscular, and quite surprisingly, the rear ones haven’t been altered.
The tuning job also includes a new set of side skirt attachments, as well as new trim on the air intakes right in front of the rear wheels. A roof scoop is part of the makeover, and it appears to be functional. The rear deck is now decorated with a large wing, and there is also a new diffuser from what we can tell. Mind you, the back end of this tuned Lamborghini Temerario is not fully visible in these images, but it is also on the more special side of things.
It looks like the ground clearance of this supercar hasn’t been altered during the tuning job. The machine features a yellow look on the outside, has some black details, and rides on new silver wheels that are larger and slightly wider than the OEM ones. Zooming in through the windows on certain pictures reveals the black and yellow interior, which appears to mix leather and Alcantara upholstery, and the Raging Bull’s logo has proudly been embroidered on the headrests.
The partially electrified oily bits haven’t been mentioned in the social media post embedded at the bottom of the page, and even if the powertrain might not have been modded, it’s not like the Lamborghini Temerario is in dire need of more oomph, is it? After all, we are still talking about a modern supercar that has the ability to sprint from 0 to 62 mph (0 to 100 kph) in just 2.7 seconds, and can keep pushing up to 213 mph (343 kph).
Photo: Instagram | kfletchphotography Lamborghini’s Temerario features a 4.0-liter twin-turbocharged V8 engine and three electric motors, for a total output of 902 horsepower (920 ps/677 kW). The ICE steams out 789 hp (800 ps/588 kW) and 530 lb-ft (730 Nm) of torque. The peak thrust is available from 4,000 to 7,000 rpm, and the maximum torque between 9,000 and 9,750 rpm.
The Lamborghini Temerario’s nuts and bolts are shared with the new Audi Nuvolari, and so far, the Raging Bull is offering its new “baby” supercar in a single flavor. However, the second body style, namely the Spyder, is about to join the lineup, and chances are it will reach dealers across the world next summer, and will also touch down officially in North America.
The open-top model will feature a power-retractable roof that should take in the region of 17 seconds to operate, and due to the extra weight, it should be a tiny bit slower than its sibling that features a fixed-roof design. The official unveiling date is being kept a secret for now, just like every detail about it, but it will get the same powertrain as the current Temerario, likely in the same configuration, with identical output and thrust.
Further down the line, Lamborghini is expected to keep expanding the Temerario family with all kinds of different versions and special editions. After all, its predecessors, the Huracan and Gallardo, were offered in all kinds of configurations. View this post on Instagram A post shared by Kyle Fletcher (@kfletchphotography)
